title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

reading.body:
An attacker exploited a vulnerability in marimo notebook software to gain initial access to a system, then deployed an AI language model agent to conduct the post-exploitation phase of the attack. The agent made real-time decisions about which systems to target and what commands to execute, rather than following a predetermined script. This suggests the AI was given access to execute commands on compromised infrastructure with minimal human oversight after the initial breach.

The attack moved through multiple systems in less than one hour, using extracted cloud credentials to retrieve SSH keys and access an internal bastion server. The agent issued commands targeting database tables that had not been enumerated in advance, and included planning comments in Chinese within the command stream, indicating the AI was reasoning through its approach in real time. The attacker also used Cloudflare Workers to distribute API calls across multiple IP addresses, defeating detection systems that track individual source IPs.

It is not established whether this represents the first such attack or how widely this technique has been adopted by threat actors. The discovery depended on forensic analysis after the fact rather than detection during the compromise itself, which suggests that deploying an AI agent with command execution capabilities on internet-connected systems creates a new attack surface that existing security monitoring was not designed to catch.

reports.title: AI agent at the wheel: How an attacker used LLMs to move from a CVE to an internal database in 4 pivots
AI Agent Conducted a Cyberattack on Its Own — It Took Less Than One Hour
Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

summary:
On May 10, 2026, the Sysdig Threat Research Team discovered an intrusion where an artificial intelligence agent controlled the attack after initial compromise. An attacker exploited a vulnerability in a marimo notebook to gain access, then extracted cloud credentials from the compromised host. Using these credentials, the attacker retrieved an SSH private key from AWS Secrets Manager and accessed an internal SSH bastion server. The entire attack chain, from initial compromise to database theft, took less than one hour to complete.

The distinctive feature of this intrusion was that an AI language model agent made real-time decisions about what to do next, rather than following a pre-written script. Key evidence includes improvised commands targeting tables the attacker had no prior knowledge of, planning comments in Chinese within the command stream, and commands shaped specifically for machine parsing and output handling. The attacker used Cloudflare Workers to distribute API calls across multiple IP addresses, defeating detection systems that rely on tracking individual source IPs. The researchers recommend immediately updating marimo to version 0.23.0 or later and rotating all credentials that may have been exposed.
